body:
## Description

This patch addresses several aspects to improve the trading account creation process:

- [x] Display Mnemonic After Account Creation:
The mnemonic now appears after successfully creating a trading account, providing users with immediate access to their mnemonic phrase.

- [x] Individual Fetching for Trading Accounts:
Replaced the bulk fetching of all trading accounts with individual fetching, optimizing the retrieval process.

- [x] Typo Corrections in onSelectTradingAddress:
Fixed typos in the implementation of onSelectTradingAddress.

- [x] Post-Account Creation Verification:
Multiple fetch operations at 8-second intervals after creating a trading account (Temp solution - Corrected an issue where the extension account was erroneously removed after creating a trading account).

- [x] Upgrade @polkadex/ux dependency and Component Renaming:
Updated the @polkadex/ux library and renamed associated components.
 
- [x] Addressed and fixed the bug related to EmptyMyAccounts component that was affecting functionality in Transfer, Balances, and Trading pages.

- [x] Profile interaction improvements (Trading accounts list, filtered local trading accounts, main account address info).

- [x]  Connect trading account interaction in trading page.

- [x] Replacement of EmptyMyAccounts Component with Connect Wallet interaction in transfer page

body:
(LINE DELTA LOOKS BIG CAUSE I UPDATED ABIS)
## Description
The most important changes on this PR are:

### Refactor of the de-serialization pool
Dropped the custom `Worker` pool with round robin implementation in favor of [`workerpool`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/workerpool)

### Found fix for web socket Max Payload Error
After finding this [stackoverflow anwser](https://eosio.stackexchange.com/questions/4189/state-history-max-payload-size-exceeded-in-jungle-block-21-289-343#4190) seemed weird we would need 8GB heap to de-serialize ship, so looking around I found this: https://www.npmjs.com/package/ws#opt-in-for-performance

Installing the recommended `bufferutil` lib allows us to have a max payload of 1.5gb on a 2gb heap.

### Improvements to state tracking variables `nextBlockRequested` & `lastBlockEmitted`

On restarts and forks, the logic of `lastBlockEmitted` & `nextBlockRequested` was causing a behavior where the first block to be emitted would be the first one to de-serialize instead the one that should go next based in incremental order.

## Change log

### (in order of appearance in `Files changed` tab)

- Stop using `main.ts` and move it to `tests/testReaderOrder.ts`
- Switch all abis to use exact same format as returned from get_abi v1 api, this includes deployed account_name info on abi
- Remove package-lock.json, only use yarn from now on
- Bump version number and add `bufferutil` dependency which allows going from 8gb to 1.5gb mem when reading specific block ranges
- Important: stop using custom `Worker` pool implementation in favour of `workerpool` library
- Create interfaces for every ds-pool call params and returns
- Start using `shm-store` for ds-pool abi data sharing
- Fail on ds-pool error instead of silent retry
- Add configurable inputQueueLimit, workerLogLevel, maxPayloadMb, action & table whitelist, speed measurer conf
- Change `lastEmittedBlock` semantics to not allow for 0 to mean ready to emit next block
- Remove old speed measurer in favour of new utils impl
- Add getter for checking if abi is ready
- Add helpers to see if user is interested in an action or table delta
- Make `start` async and query node for specificed range on start if aplicable
- Set `nextBlockRequested` to `lastEmittedBlock` on restarts
- Do another check on data returned from the initial ship message to see if node has requested range state, also set start block and end block if -1 passed & init `lastEmittedBlock` & `nextBlockRequested`
- Set `lastEmittedBlock` to `lastNonForked` on forks
- Use new `workerpool` based ds-pool on `decodeShipData`
- Create helper for emitting a block an letting al state tracking vars in a correct state and use it when necesary
- Move utils to their own module
- Update yarn.lock

author: igchor
body:
I've noticed there are not too many benchmarks in this repo. I wanted to port some of the existing ones so a comparison can be made with 'native' implementations. This benchmark is based on https://github.com/oneapi-src/oneTBB/tree/master/examples/migration/recursive_fibonacci 

This is, of course, a very inefficient way to calculate Fibonacci numbers, but it is quite a good benchmark for use cases where new tasks are created recursively. I've implemented this using a custom sender. This is probably not the most idiomatic way but I couldn't figure out how to achieve the same performance by just using existing algorithms (and without start_detached) - perhaps you have some ideas? Any feedback is welcomed.

When running on my computer (on i9-7940X) I get:
```
# ./examples/example.benchmark.fibonacci 16 46 10 static
Avg time: 4377ms. Result: 1836311903
# ./examples/example.benchmark.fibonacci 16 46 10 tbb
Avg time: 763ms. Result: 1836311903
```

When running the 'native' tbb example (from the tbb repo) I get:
```
Fibonacci two tasks impl N = 1836311903 Avg time = 311 ms
Fibonacci single task impl N = 1836311903 Avg time = 310 ms
```

body:
This fixes up a number of minor issues across the user profile, the authenticated landing page, and the institutional details page. This isn't meant to be a fix for everything, but it does make it so those three pages now work for the primary use case.

Remade [from this PR](https://github.com/cfpb/sbl-frontend/pull/112#issuecomment-1874455769).

## Changes
- Use `fetchAssociatedInstitutions` with the new `domain` query param to limit choices to only ones that the user is associated with on the UserProfile page
- Limit zod typing to only MVP fields to stop form submission interruptions
- Force an auth token refresh after user object is updated to allow the server to be the source of truth for the landing page instead of the `formState` that is limited to being transitory and won't work on page refresh
- Made a new fetch handler for `fetchAssociatedInstitutions`
- Use `fetchAssociatedInstitutions` to populate the shared landing page institutions
- Fix review institutions page bug that prevented rendering by changing `hq_address_state` to `hq_address_state_code` which is the property the server sends

## How to test this PR

1. Start with a user that has an email with a domain that is associated with a financial institution
2. Log in, and you should see the complete user profile page
3. Add a first name, last name, and select an institution
4. Submit the form and you should be on the landing page
5. You should see your institution listed at the bottom of the page
6. Clicking that institution should bring you to that institution's details page

## Screenshots

author: dwnusbaum
body:
See https://github.com/jenkinsci/pipeline-build-step-plugin/pull/128#discussion_r1427007989 and the next comment.

If `FlowExecution.saveActions` is called for a Pipeline with a completed execution, in some cases (all cases as of https://github.com/jenkinsci/workflow-cps-plugin/pull/807), the save will be a no-op and nothing will be written to disk. Notably this method is called implicitly when updating actions on a `FlowNode` or when explicitly calling `FlowNode.save`.

We should throw an error in this case instead to make it easier for developers to detect and identify any issues. Generally speaking, to persist metadata for a possibly-completed build, you should use an `Action` on the `Run` that stores `FlowNode.getId` as needed.

* [x] Run PCT to check if this affects tests in significant plugins (https://github.com/jenkinsci/bom/pull/2785)
* [x] Add test (`CpsFlowExecutionTest.flowNodesCantBeSavedAfterExecutionCompletes`)

## Summary

### Human Summary

This PR allows you to merge `N` observables into a single observable via the `Merge` function with takes a slice of observables and a bool as to whether the merged observable should *fail fast* or not. This means should the merged observable fail (call `UnsubsribeAll` the first time an observable its merging errors or to go on notifying using the others.

author: sekqies
body:
Esse texto, também, explica o que foi feito no commit passado.

A utilização do Algebrite mostrou uma diminuição considerável na performance, visto que ele realiza a expansão de polinômios, entre outras operações desnecessárias.

Nesses commits:
1. Foi removida a utilização do Algebrite.run para encontrar os valores (visto que ele não sabe lidar bem com números complexos)
2. Foi criada funções próprias para cálculo de funções complexas (comp_{sen,cos,log,exp,pol}
3. Criado método para ignorar as expansões de polinômios, ao substituir o polinômio por um caractere arbitrário.


TODO: 
- Tentar achar uma forma sem o algebrite de achar valores reais e imaginários
- cosh, senh, atan, tan
- Criar algoritmo próprio para multiplicação
- Executar algoritmo para operações repetidas (útil para z^z)
- Melhor alguns dos regexes para comp_exp e comp_pol

author: gianm
body:
It was using virtualColumns.getColumnCapabilities, which only returns capabilities for virtual columns, not regular columns. The effect of this is that expression filters (and in some cases, arrayContainsElement filters) would build value matchers rather than use indexes.

I think this is a performance regression since #12315, which added the getColumnCapabilities method to BitmapIndexSelector, and included the same implementation as exists in the code today.

This error is easy to make due to the design of virtualColumns.getColumnCapabilities, so to help avoid it in the future, this patch renames the method to getColumnCapabilitiesWithoutFallback to emphasize that it does not return capabilities for regular columns.

author: dewert99
body:
Fixes #188

I think I was able to get a decent version of push/pop working. I added a few tests for it but it may still be buggy, so we should probably add some more before merging this.

I added an associate type `UndoLog` to the `Analysis` trait to allow users to opt-in to the extra cost tracking this information. Ideally, it would default to `()` which restores the old behaviour, but unfortunately, associated type defaults are not stable so this is a breaking change. This idea could also be used for explanations so calling an explanation-related method when explanations are disabled would be a compile-time error rather than a run-time error. 

Calling `pop` currently requires explanations to be enabled since it uses `id_to_node`, the `UndoLog` could store its own copy of this information but this would be redundant if explanations and push/pop were both enabled. Another idea would be to store each uncanonical id's original node directly in the egraph, this would allow us to avoid storing nodes in `EClass.parents`, `EGraph.pending`, and `EGraph.analysis_pending`, eliminate `ExplainNode.node`, and make the `Egraph::id_to_X` methods not require explanations to be enabled. Would it be worth doing a separate PR for this first?

Calling `pop` also currently requires that the analysis doesn't do anything, as I am still trying to figure out the best way to revert an arbitrary merge implementation.

Calling `push` requires `pending`/`analysis_pending` to be empty, users can deal with this by calling `rebuild` before `push` but technically calling `process_unions` is sufficient. I've been wondering if it is worth making `process_unions` public since `rebuild_classes` is only necessary for `Searcher`s. This would also allow `pop` to be optimized for the case where `rebuild_classes` hasn't been called since the last `push`.

author: tuvus
body:
This fixes an error that was reported on Discord.
The problem came from the caching feature in #10776. 
In the bug, a worker valued the tile and did not go to it. Instead, a military unit that can build roads and forts looked at the cache of the previous worker and tried to build an improvement it couldn't build.

The solution is more of a temporary fix to a problem with caching and the difference in the buildings that workers can build. We just check if the current worker can build that improvement. This solution works as of now only because the workers (in this case, military units) with the smaller pool of buildings that they can build are a subset of the buildings of the regular worker's pool. And since the regular workers move before the military workers there isn't any clashing yet. 

But what if we have two civilian workers that can build different types of buildings...

author: ianarawjo
body:
A longstanding issue has been a huge (1sec or higher) lag when clicking the Run button of Prompt Nodes. It wasn't what I thought it was ---the issue came from calling state-setting properties, and forcing back-to-back re-renders, inside the progress listener callback (used to update the various progress bars in the Prompt Node). The solution was to debounce (here 30ms) progress bar UI updates.

This update also removes debounce for genAI in Items nodes, which was causing a delay of the re-render.

author: thelnfamous1
body:
Added a check for `PartEntity` during the filtering of the gathered `Entity` list during `EntityVoidPortal#tick`. You have already established that multipart entities should not be teleported via these portals (`e.getParts() != null`), so I am simply reinforcing this check by filtering out their `PartEntity`s.

The original error was a result of `EntityVoidPortal#teleportEntityFromDimension` creating a new `Entity` from the previous one's `EntityType`, but the `EntityType` of a `PartEntity` is the same as its parent mob (For example, the `EntityType` of an `EntityLaviathinPart` is the same as `EntityLaviathin`). So these `PartEntity`s are getting copied over to the other dimension as brand new instances of their parent mob.
